name: Genetic Infertility

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic genetic variants associated with infertility
Abnormal semen parameters including azoospermia or oligospermia in males
Evidence of primary ovarian insufficiency or diminished ovarian reserve in females
Positive family history of infertility or related genetic disorders
Abnormal reproductive hormone levels consistent with gonadal dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic genetic variant plus clinical evidence of gonadal dysfunction (abnormal semen analysis in males or ovarian insufficiency in females)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic testing with clinical and laboratory findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Complete absence of sperm in semen due to genetic causes
Premature loss of ovarian function before age 40

searchTerms: chromosome problems affecting sperm or egg production

common.notes: Menstrual irregularities due to ovarian dysfunction
Reduced testicular size associated with impaired spermatogenesis

occasional.notes: Breast tissue enlargement in males with certain chromosomal abnormalities
Late onset of secondary sexual characteristics
Reduced function of gonads leading to low sex hormone levels

rare.notes: Associated with cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) mutations
searchTerms: congenital absence of sperm transport tube

rare.notes: Seen in syndromic forms of genetic infertility
Present in some syndromic infertility disorders

laboratory: Elevated serum FSH and LH levels
Low serum testosterone or estradiol levels
imaging: Testicular ultrasound showing atrophy or structural abnormalities
Pelvic ultrasound demonstrating reduced ovarian volume
genetic: Mutations in genes such as CFTR, NR5A1, and others related to gametogenesis
Microdeletions in Y chromosome azoospermia factor (AZF) regions
other: Family history of infertility or related genetic syndromes
Physical examination findings consistent with syndromic features

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of sperm in testicular tissue

redFlags: Complete absence of sperm in semen without obstruction
Elevated gonadotropins indicating primary gonadal failure
Family history of genetic syndromes associated with infertility
references: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine. Diagnostic evaluation of the infertile male: a committee opinion. Fertil Steril. 2015.
Krausz C, Riera-Escamilla A. Genetics of male infertility. Nat Rev Urol. 2018.
